title: Hilbert's 17th: The Motzkin Polynomial Is Not a Sum of Squares of Polynomials
description: The Motzkin polynomial M = x⁴y² + x²y⁴ − 3x²y² + 1 is nonnegative on all of ℝ² yet is the canonical example of a nonnegative polynomial that is NOT a sum of squares of polynomials — the negative half of Hilbert's 17th problem, which forces the passage to sums of squares of rational functions. The parent entry hilbert-17 carries this fact as the axiom motzkin_not_sos_polynomial_aux; the sibling entry hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-01 lists discharging it as an open question. This entry supplies a fully elementary, 0-axiom proof. Suppose M = Σᵢ qᵢ². (1) Degree bound: the degree-2D homogeneous component of a sum of squares is Σ (top form)², which over ℝ vanishes only if every top form does; since M has total degree 6, every qᵢ has total degree ≤ 3. (2) Pure-axis vanishing: comparing the x⁶, x⁴, x² (and y⁶, y⁴, y²) coefficients on both sides, and using that a sum of real squares is 0 only if each term is, forces the coefficients of x, x², x³ (and y, y², y³) in every qᵢ to vanish. (3) The x²y² coefficient: with the degree bound and pure-axis vanishing, the only pair of monomials of qᵢ multiplying to x²y² is (xy)·(xy), so [x²y²] qᵢ² = ([xy] qᵢ)². Summing: −3 = [x²y²] M = Σᵢ ([xy] qᵢ)² ≥ 0, a contradiction. No real-closed-field machinery, no Newton-polytope theory — only multivariate-polynomial coefficient extraction (coeff_mul), homogeneous components, and the order structure of ℝ.

mainTheorems.name: motzkin_not_sos
mainTheorems.description: The Motzkin polynomial is not a sum of squares of polynomials: there is no finite family q with M = Σ qᵢ². Discharges the parent axiom motzkin_not_sos_polynomial_aux with 0 axioms.

mainTheorems.name: degree_bound
mainTheorems.description: If Σ qᵢ² = M (total degree ≤ 6), then every qᵢ has total degree ≤ 3 — the no-cancellation property of leading forms of a sum of squares.

mainTheorems.name: topsq
mainTheorems.description: The degree-2D homogeneous component of p² equals the square of the degree-D component, whenever D bounds the total degree of p. The product-of-leading-forms identity underlying the degree bound.

mainTheorems.name: pureX_extract
mainTheorems.description: Under the degree bound, the x^{2n} coefficient of qᵢ² collapses to ([xⁿ] qᵢ)²; the y-mirror is pureY_extract. Drives the chain that kills all pure-axis coefficients.

mainTheorems.name: coeff22_sq
mainTheorems.description: The crux: with the degree bound and pure-axis vanishing, [x²y²] qᵢ² = ([xy] qᵢ)², because (xy)·(xy) is the only surviving antidiagonal pair. Summing gives −3 = Σ ([xy] qᵢ)² ≥ 0.

mainTheorems.name: sum_sq_eq_zero
mainTheorems.description: A finite sum of squares of real multivariate polynomials is zero only if each summand is zero — proved by evaluating at every point (MvPolynomial.funext) and using the order structure of ℝ.

overview.historicalContext: Hilbert's 17th problem (1900) asked whether every polynomial nonnegative on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is a sum of squares of rational functions; Emil Artin answered it affirmatively in 1927 using the Artin–Schreier theory of real-closed fields. The qualifier 'rational functions' is essential: Hilbert had already shown (non-constructively, 1888) that nonnegative polynomials need not be sums of squares of polynomials. The first explicit counterexample, the Motzkin polynomial $M = x^4y^2 + x^2y^4 - 3x^2y^2 + 1$, was produced by T. S. Motzkin in 1967 — it is nonnegative everywhere (by the AM–GM inequality on $x^4y^2, x^2y^4, 1$) yet provably not a sum of squares of polynomials. It became the canonical witness that polynomial-SOS is strictly weaker than nonnegativity, motivating the passage to rational SOS. This entry supplies a fully elementary, 0-axiom Lean formalization of Motzkin's non-representability, discharging the parent entry's axiom motzkin_not_sos_polynomial_aux.
overview.problemStatement: The Motzkin polynomial $M = x^4y^2 + x^2y^4 - 3x^2y^2 + 1 \in \mathbb{R}[x,y]$ is nonnegative on all of $\mathbb{R}^2$. The claim formalized here is that $M$ is NOT a sum of squares of polynomials: there is no finite family $q_1, \dots, q_k \in \mathbb{R}[x,y]$ with $M = \sum_i q_i^2$. In Lean: $\neg\, \mathrm{IsSOS}\ \mathrm{motzkin}$ over $\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\ (\mathrm{Fin}\ 2)\ \mathbb{R}$, where IsSOS unfolds to the same sum-of-squares predicate used by the parent entry. This is the negative half of Hilbert's 17th problem for the canonical example.
overview.proofStrategy: A self-contained coefficient argument on $\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\ (\mathrm{Fin}\ 2)\ \mathbb{R}$, needing no real-closed-field theory and no general Newton-polytope machinery, in three moves. (1) Degree bound: if $M = \sum_i q_i^2$ then each $q_i$ has total degree $\le 3$ — the degree-$2D$ homogeneous component of a square equals the square of its degree-$D$ component (lemma topsq), and over $\mathbb{R}$ a sum of squares of nonzero forms cannot cancel (lemma sum_sq_eq_zero, via MvPolynomial.funext), so the leading form of degree-6 $M$ forces each $q_i$ to degree $\le 3$. (2) Pure-axis vanishing: comparing the $x^6, x^4, x^2$ (and $y^6, y^4, y^2$) coefficients on both sides expresses each as a sum of real squares that must be zero, killing the coefficients of $x, x^2, x^3$ (and $y, y^2, y^3$) in every $q_i$ via the chains $x^6 \to x^4 \to x^2$ and $y^6 \to y^4 \to y^2$ (pureX_extract / pureY_extract). (3) The crux: with the degree bound and pure-axis vanishing, the only antidiagonal pair of monomials of $q_i$ multiplying to $x^2y^2$ is $(xy)\cdot(xy)$, so $[x^2y^2]\,q_i^2 = ([xy]\,q_i)^2$ (lemma coeff22_sq). Summing gives $-3 = [x^2y^2]\,M = \sum_i ([xy]\,q_i)^2 \ge 0$, a contradiction. Each antidiagonal coefficient sum collapses to a single surviving term via Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem.
keyInsights: Nonnegativity is strictly weaker than being a polynomial sum of squares. The Motzkin polynomial is nonnegative on $\mathbb{R}^2$ (by AM–GM on $x^4y^2, x^2y^4, 1$) yet is not a sum of squares of polynomials — the gap that makes Hilbert's 17th nontrivial and forces the answer into rational SOS.

A sum of squares of real polynomials is zero only if each summand is zero (sum_sq_eq_zero). Proved by evaluating at every point via MvPolynomial.funext (valid over the infinite domain $\mathbb{R}$) and using the order structure of $\mathbb{R}$ — this is the elementary positivity engine behind both the degree bound and the final contradiction.

Leading forms of a sum of squares cannot cancel. The degree-$2D$ homogeneous component of $p^2$ is exactly $(\text{degree-}D\text{ component of } p)^2$ (topsq), so the degree-6 top form of $M$ being a sum of squares of top forms bounds every $q_i$ to total degree $\le 3$ (degree_bound).

Coefficient extraction collapses to a single antidiagonal term. The general MvPolynomial.coeff_mul sum over the Finsupp antidiagonal reduces, under the degree bound and pure-axis vanishing, to one surviving square: $[x^{2n}]\,q_i^2 = ([x^n]\,q_i)^2$ and $[x^2y^2]\,q_i^2 = ([xy]\,q_i)^2$.

The contradiction is purely sign-based. After the degree and pure-axis kills, $-3 = [x^2y^2]\,M = \sum_i ([xy]\,q_i)^2 \ge 0$ — a negative number equal to a sum of real squares — with no real-closed-field machinery or Newton-polytope theory invoked.

The proof is 0-axiom and reusable. #print axioms motzkin_not_sos reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (no sorryAx, no native_decide). It packages transferable infrastructure (topsq, sum_sq_eq_zero, the pure-axis and $x^2y^2$ extraction lemmas) applicable to other extremal PSD-but-not-SOS forms such as the Robinson polynomial, and discharges the parent entry's axiom motzkin_not_sos_polynomial_aux.

conclusion.summary: A 427-line, 0-sorry, 0-axiom formalization that the Motzkin polynomial is not a sum of squares of polynomials — the negative half of Hilbert's 17th problem for the canonical example. Complements the positive-side sibling (a rational SOS certificate) and discharges the parent entry's axiom motzkin_not_sos_polynomial_aux by an elementary degree-and-coefficient argument.
conclusion.implications: Together with sibling hilbert-17-oq-03-oq-01 (Motzkin IS a sum of squares of rational functions), this closes both directions for the Motzkin example: PSD, not polynomial-SOS, but rational-SOS — Hilbert's 17th in microcosm, fully machine-checked with 0 axioms. The proof also packages reusable infrastructure: topsq (leading form of a square), sum_sq_eq_zero (a sum of squares of real polynomials is zero only if each is), and the pure-axis / x²y² extraction lemmas, which transfer to other extremal PSD-not-SOS forms.

sections.summary: pureX_extract / pureY_extract collapse the x^{2n}/y^{2n} antidiagonal sums to single squares; coeff22_sq does the same for x²y². motzkin_not_sos chains them: the degree bound gives the degree-≥4 vanishing, the x⁶→x⁴→x² and y⁶→y⁴→y² chains kill all pure-axis coefficients, and then [x²y²] M = Σ ([xy] qᵢ)² ≥ 0 contradicts [x²y²] M = −3.
